steps.text: The fingers have contact with the lever. I’m using a short pulling motion because the wrist is near its rotation limit in this posture.
The lever is still upright after that attempt. I’ll adjust the approach angle to give the wrist more room, then make another controlled grasp.
The grasp slipped before the lever moved far enough. I’ll seat it deeper between the finger pads and retry with smaller motions.
I’m checking the opposite direction with a small motion. The previous pulls left the lever close to upright, so its allowed direction is still uncertain.
The lever resists the backward motion, and the pinch keeps slipping during a pull. I’ll move the closed fingers around its side and use direct contact to push it forward.
The lever is still upright. I’m moving above it to reach its back side without dragging the fingers across the shaft.
The spout is obstructing the wrist from above. I’m switching to an approach from the right, which should also let the finger pads push across the lever’s arc.
